spans.s: √div\nsee √dīv1\nNo root √div 'shine' exists as such in the language, except so far as it may be inferable from the noun dív or dyú V.+, divít RV., and the (in that case, secondary) root dyut. With all these the root dīv 'play' has nothing to do.

√dīv1 'play'
present: [4.] dī́vyati etc. V.+ dī́vyate etc. B.+ divyati etc. 
perfect: didéva 
aorist: [3.] adīdivat -- [5.] adevīt etc. 
future: [1.] deviṣyati etc. E.+ adeviṣyat -- [2.] devitā 
verbal: dyūtá AV.+ dyūna devitum E.+ devitvā dyūtvā -dī́vya 
secondary: intensive: dedīv- -- desiderative: dideviṣa- dudyūṣa- dudyūṣaya- -- causative: devayati etc. 
derivatives: dī́v dyū́ -dī́van V. dīvana C. -deva B. dévana V.+ devin AV.+ devitavya E. devitṛ E.+ -dyūtyà RV. 
Proper form, dīū; and it has nothing to do with the so-called root div 'shine', which is diu.

√dīv2 'lament'
present: [1.] devati E.+ devate 
[perfect: dideva adidevat adeviṣṭa deviṣyate devitā ]
verbal: dyūna B.+ devitum 
secondary: causative: devayati etc. E.+ devayate E.+ 
derivatives: -deva -devaka C. -devin E. -devana C. 
Only with pari (unless in ādyūna); hence perhaps a peculiar specialization of meaning of √1dīv (paridyūna 'played out'?). At any rate, rather dīv than div, on account of the long ū in dyūna.
